definitions.explanation: An organ or group of cells in the body that produces and secretes substances such as hormones, sweat, or saliva. Used in medical and biological contexts.

examples.japanese: {甲状|こうじょう}{腺|せん}の{検査|けんさ}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I had my thyroid gland examined.

examples.japanese: {汗|あせ}{腺|せん}から{汗|あせ}が{分泌|ぶんぴつ}される。
examples.english: Sweat is secreted from the sweat glands.

examples.japanese: {唾液|だえき}{腺|せん}が{腫|は}れて{食事|しょくじ}のときに{痛|いた}みを{感|かん}じるので、{病院|びょういん}に{行|い}くことにした。
examples.english: My salivary glands are swollen and I feel pain when eating, so I decided to go to the hospital.

notes:
USAGE:
Rarely used alone; almost always appears as a suffix combined with the type of gland. Note the kanji {腺|せん} contains the {月|にくづき} radical (flesh/body) plus {泉|いずみ} (spring), reflecting its meaning as a bodily source of fluids.

COMPOUNDS:
- {甲状|こうじょう}{腺|せん} (thyroid gland)
- {汗|あせ}{腺|せん} (sweat gland)
- {唾液|だえき}{腺|せん} (salivary gland)
- {乳|にゅう}{腺|せん} (mammary gland)
- {前立|ぜんりつ}{腺|せん} (prostate gland)
- リンパ{腺|せん} (lymph gland)
